story.fullStory:
Glen Campbell's "Wichita Lineman" reached #3 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Wichita Lineman" is a 1968 song written by Jimmy Webb for American country music artist Glen Campbell, who recorded it backed by members of the Wrecking Crew.

Widely covered by other artists, it has been called "the first existential country song".

In 2021, Rolling Stone magazine's list of the "500 Greatest Songs of All Time" ranked "Wichita Lineman" at number 206.

The song peaked at #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 15 weeks on the chart.

approvedFacts.text: "Wichita Lineman" is a 1968 song written by Jimmy Webb for American country music artist Glen Campbell, who recorded it backed by members of the Wrecking Crew.
Widely covered by other artists, it has been called "the first existential country song".
In 2021, Rolling Stone magazine's list of the "500 Greatest Songs of All Time" ranked "Wichita Lineman" at number 206.
The song peaked at #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 15 weeks on the chart.
Wichita Lineman is the eleventh studio album by American singer-guitarist Glen Campbell, released in 1968 by Capitol Records.
In 2000, the single Wichita Lineman was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.
Glen Travis Campbell (April 22, 1936 – August 8, 2017) was an American country musician and actor.
